module.label: Browser effect channels
module.description: Isolated per-project audio and visual-effect handshakes.

flows.label: A browser effect is played
flows.detail: The browser draws from current audio position for the entire sound duration and clears on the owning audio's ended event. Pause and seek reconstruct the same frame; the stock renderer clips artwork to the gameplay perimeter; feature presentations own their own layout. Approved arena/racing/muffin owners remain. The 85 other cues have contextual subjects, individually arranged supporting casts and staggered entrances. Pedro has seven dancing raccoons and a DJ stage; sad violin has an orchestra, glass cameos, notes and a score. No worker, source controller or animation timer is added. Feature-owned presentations may publish explicitly named artwork under token-scoped registration during startup; teardown cannot unregister a newer owner. The shared HTTP owner serves original file bytes, including JSON manifests, while serializing state API objects separately, without importing feature policy. Hooray keeps original audio and current gain while a dedicated bounded native-alpha foil renderer draws corner bursts, sparse confetti across the picture and gold border ribbons; original chroma-filter and transform settings remain preserved. The current culture pass authors distinct native performances for all 30 sounds behind ! 2 # Z T t h H after reviewing their actual local clips. Party/reaction owners supply contextual subjects, causal jokes, finite acts and peripheral sets; supporting cameos preserve approved main shows and recognizable photographic casts. Precomputed original-media envelopes and measured cadence guide illustration only, without live DSP or a new clock. Original audio duration, currentTime, pause, channel identity, personal data and cleanup remain unchanged. The follow-up choreography gives long sounds finite actions and held consequences: prop losses/catches, food grabs, a stolen Pedro record, and a snapped violin string. MuffinShow owns the local clip's final-die cue at approximately 6.24 seconds; all eight muffins collapse together and remain down until the original sound ends. Its 55-ms release retains the punchline without stretching audio. All acts reconstruct solely from currentTime, including backward seeks and fresh replays. The further meme-action pass adds Cena invisibility/autofocus, the hindsight slip, coffee-denial toaster jump, physical spill/failed undo, precise mute click, warded ambush, Starman last-hit deflection, Gary snack, Quack popup escape and the frog microphone topple. Cue-specific contact anchors live in culture-contacts.js and are shared with finite geometry review; no simulations, independent clocks or gameplay commands are introduced. The channel owns a revision and bounded one-second condition wait. Playback/control mutations wake serialized browser requests immediately without holding the state lock while waiting. Legacy reads remain immediate; browser teardown aborts its request and cancels its timer. A two-second transport deadline bounds hung requests.

steps.label: Use the project browser channel
steps.detail: Mom Frog's extracted photographic views and pond props use the same channel and original croak duration; its finite offline audio cleanup preserves saved faders. The existing random hotkey 2 queue uses five independent three-pose character borders: Tom button/popcorn, Gary meow/snacks, duck desktop, Bonk mallet crew and Piuw space cadets. They follow each sound's actual position/duration; asset identities, random selection and saved audio settings remain unchanged. Piuw has traveling plasma ribbons, zaps and shock rings; Frog has flowing pond currents, splash fans and croak waves. Explicit finite Piuw/Frog audio cleanup preserves original and previous versions outside the checkout, reprocesses the original backup, validates candidates, copies Frog video and never normalizes or changes faders. Finite Chromium QA verifies actual audio playback, transparency, motion, pause determinism and cleanup.

steps.label: Wait for ready OBS browser
steps.detail: The browser waits for metadata and atlas readiness. Visible sources draw and clear a zero-time warm-up frame, then yield one presentation frame with a 100-ms fallback for a suspended browser clock. Hidden sources skip painting. A replaced or stopped audio identity cannot continue delayed startup.

steps.label: Wait for current playback ID
steps.detail: Current audio time drives every live border frame. Under-1.5-second BorderShow cues opt into 12-ms attack/18-ms release; other presentations retain their existing fades. Pause freezes audio and drawing together. Invisible sources cancel canvas frames while audio, heartbeats and completion continue; visible return draws current audio time. Finite review exports use original audio, one A/V timeline, exact-duration frame sampling and external controls; looping belongs only to the review page.

steps.label: Stop or acknowledge cleanup
steps.detail: The owning audio ended event clears the live canvas and acknowledges its actual playback ID. Replaced IDs cannot finish a newer request. Decoded-frame review QA verifies visible onset, complete playback, one audible preview, pause, one-shot cleanup and A/V start/cutoff alignment.

flows.label: Shared painted-world mechanics

trigger.label: A feature loads the public mechanics

flows.detail: AmbientClock plans finite weighted phrases with recent-guest weighting and soft pressure, retains at most four plans and starts no timer. PaintedPatch decodes a small crop once, caches fixed triangle connections and source coefficients, and reuses coordinate buffers for each feature-provided deformation. Drawing order and mesh detail stay unchanged; disposal releases the canvas and all mesh buffers. Shared helpers own no theme, cast, live display placement or scene policy. Finite build publication copies original mechanic bytes and records canonical hashes.

steps.label: Accept feature-supplied data
steps.detail: The caller owns palette, subjects, landmarks, cue weights and rendering lifecycle.

steps.label: Reuse bounded cached mechanics
steps.detail: No socket, audio channel, playback worker or independent animation timer is allocated.

steps.label: Dispose owned caches
steps.detail: The caller tears down clock history and decoded patch canvases.
